claims.text: Pre-depositing a thin aluminum layer on CoCrFeNi will promote in situ formation of an alumina-based tribofilm during sliding.
The alumina-based tribofilm will be stable and protective from room temperature to 800 °C.
The alumina-based tribofilm will maintain low friction and wear over the full temperature range.
Untreated CoCrFeNi exhibits moderate oxidation and wear during sliding at different temperatures.
A thin aluminum coating or targeted aluminum surface doping can be applied to CoCrFeNi before sliding.
Sliding of the Al-treated surface will produce a continuous tribo-oxide layer predominantly composed of Al2O3.
The tribo-oxide layer will bond strongly to the CoCrFeNi matrix.
At lower temperatures, the thin aluminum layer will minimally alter surface friction.
Sliding-induced heating will cause aluminum to react with oxygen and form an alumina tribo-oxide film.
The resulting alumina tribo-oxide film will be hard and have low shear resistance.
The alumina film will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reducing direct contact will suppress adhesive and abrasive wear.
Al-treated CoCrFeNi will have significantly lower coefficients of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi from 25 °C to 800 °C.
Al-treated CoCrFeNi will have significantly lower wear rates than untreated CoCrFeNi from 25 °C to 800 °C.
The friction and wear benefits will become more pronounced at higher temperatures because oxide formation is enhanced.
The proposed performance is bounded to dry sliding in air under moderate contact loads.
Performance may differ under lubrication or in inert atmospheres.
Aluminum-layer thickness will affect adhesion and tribo-oxide formation and therefore requires optimization.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says the aluminum layer minimally alters friction at lower temperatures, whereas the predicted outcome requires a significant friction reduction consistently across the entire range, including room temperature.
